The Senate voted 47-41 to confirm Sonderling. The vote came as lawmakers prepared to leave Washington to campaign ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Sonderling has held several positions at the Labor Department and was previously a Republican member of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. He served as deputy secretary during Trump's second term before becoming acting secretary in April. His confirmation comes at a time when the Labor Department is dealing with questions around artificial intelligence, worker training, employment data and the changing nature of jobs in the US. Sonderling discussed the impact of AI on American workers during his confirmation hearing in July. He said the Labor Department was collecting information from companies and unions about how they were using AI. The Bureau of Labor Statistics would review the information, with the department looking to use the data to help direct job-training money to states.
